what_it_does: Spiking neural networks are a biologically-inspired alternative to standard neural networks: instead of continuous values, neurons fire discrete pulses at specific times. This sparse, event-driven computation uses far less energy but is harder to optimize. To shrink a spiking network efficiently, you can prune (remove) neurons, reduce connection weights, or lower firing thresholds—but these three dimensions interact. This paper presents a dynamic joint pruning framework that adjusts all three together based on real-time feedback about computational cost. It introduces temporal attention batch normalization, which learns time-dependent scaling factors, and dynamically recalibrates importance scores as pruning progresses.
